title: Kernel coalescing and power-aware concurrency for low-latency inference (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This doc proposes a pragmatic, testable set of heuristics and operational knobs for combining kernel coalescing, per-GPU power caps, and concurrency limits to minimize 99th- and 95th-percentile latency for interactive text and chat requests while preserving cost-efficiency. It focuses on heterogenous pools (A100, H100, L4, MI300) and interactions with KV cache reuse and batching.

Motivation / Problem statement:
- Production workloads show that naive concurrency/autoscaling plus static GPU clocks leads to large tail-latency spikes under mixed sequences and mixed-model loads.
- Some kernels (attention / rotary / kv gather) become bottlenecks when many small requests interleave; naively increasing concurrency increases memory bandwidth contention and thermal throttling.
- Different GPU families respond differently to power limits and frequency changes (A100: more stable under power cap; H100: aggressive boost at high clocks; L4: optimized for batch throughput but weaker single-stream performance; MI300: CPU-like behavior for memory ops).
- We need a runtime strategy that dynamically coalesces work into kernels that preserve low latency for small requests while enabling higher utilization on bursts without pushing GPUs into thermal/power regimes that increase tail latency.

Design goals (ranked):
1) Keep p50/p95/p99 below configured SLOs for interactive endpoints.
2) Reduce per-token cost by improving packing for bursty workloads without hurting latency for single-request flows.
3) Avoid repeated fallback flapping (model or region fallbacks) caused by temporary bursts; prefer short-term local throttles.
4) Be conservative on MI300 unless tests show safe thermal headroom.

Key concepts / building blocks:
- Kernel coalescing: Combine small, compatible work items into a single kernel dispatch when latency headroom exists. The runtime will coalesce along 3 axes: batch dim, sequence prefixes (KV cache reuse), and attention-query groups.
- Power-aware concurrency (PAC): For each GPU, maintain a dynamic concurrency limit informed by a power and temperature budget. PAC prevents the runtime from launching so many streams that the card hits a high-power regime that raises latency.
- Fast probe: A short-lived probe mode to test whether additional coalescing or higher concurrency improves latency or triggers adverse thermal behavior. Probes are conducted at controlled cadence per-worker.
- KV affinity gating: Treat requests which hit KV cache as coalescing-friendly; they contribute less to memory pressure and can be batched more aggressively.

Heuristic rules (initial version):
1) Baseline concurrency per GPU (base_concurrency):
   - A100: 6 simultaneous inference contexts per GPU
   - H100: 8 simultaneous inference contexts per GPU
   - L4: 4 simultaneous contexts
   - MI300: 3 simultaneous contexts
   Rationale: conservative starting point derived from lab runs focusing on p99 for 8k-ish models. These are tunable flags.

2) Power cap thresholds (soft limits):
   - If GPU power draw > 85% of configured card TDP for longer than 3s, decrement concurrency by 1 and start a 15s cool-down timer.
   - If temperature > 80C for > 5s, do an immediate 2-step concurrency reduction and reduce clock boost policy for 30s.
   - If power < 60% and latency headroom exists for p95 < target/2, probe an increase in concurrency by +1.

3) Kernel coalescing policy:
   - Always coalesce requests that are KV-cache hits and have identical sequence-length buckets within 20% length variance. Coalesce up to coalescing_max_batch (default 32 for A100/H100, 16 for L4, 8 for MI300).
   - For cold requests (no KV hit) prefer small micro-batches (1-4) and avoid coalescing across different model variants.
   - Prefer prefix coalescing: if 2+ requests share a long common prefix in tokenization, prioritize merging into a single kernel using prefix-reuse path.

4) Probe behavior and rollback:
   - Probes last a configurable short period (2-10s). During a probe, mark a small fraction of worker slots as trial slots (default 1 per GPU). If probe increases p95 by > 15% or raises power draw by > 7% compared to baseline, rollback. Use exponential backoff on probe cadence if failures observed.

5) KV cache heuristics:
   - If prefix reuse > 60% across last 60s, increase coalescing_max_batch by +8 (bounded by per-GPU limit).
   - If KV eviction rate increases or memory alloc failure observed, reduce coalescing aggressiveness immediately and trigger a memory-pressure alert.

Ops knobs / config flags (exposed):
- base_concurrency_{gpu_type}: integer
- pac_power_threshold_pct: integer (default 85)
- pac_temp_threshold_c: integer (default 80)
- coalescing_max_batch_{gpu_type}: integer
- coalescing_seq_length_tolerance_pct: integer (default 20)
- probe_duration_s: integer
- probe_fraction_per_gpu: float (default 0.02)
- kv_coalesce_boost_pct: integer (default 8)
- pac_cooldown_s: integer (default 15)

Instrumentation and metrics to add (must be surfaced in Console):
- per-GPU: power_draw_watts, sustained_power_pct_tdp, gpu_temp_c, active_contexts, kernel_dispatches_per_s, avg_kernel_latency_ms, kernel_tail_latency_99_ms
- per-worker: coalesced_batch_size_histogram, kv_hit_rate, memory_pressure_events, probe_success_rate
- per-endpoint: p50/p95/p99 generation latency with tag whether coalesced or not, tokens_per_sec, cost_per_token_estimate
- alerts: rapid_power_rise (>10% in 1s), repeated probe failures (>3 in 5m), kv_evictions_high (>threshold)

Measurement plan (lab -> canary -> rollout):
1) Lab: run controlled experiments on representative hardware for 48h per GPU type with synthetic mixes: 80% single-turn chat small requests, 15% medium multi-turn, 5% long context. Measure tails and power/thermal behavior.
2) Canary: enable policy in a small dedicated pool (10 gpus across regions) for low-risk prod namespace. Observe for 72h, watch for flapping/concurrency oscillation.
3) Incremental rollout: if canary stable, roll out by 10% of capacity every 24h. Continue to tune base_concurrency per fleet.

Failure modes and mitigations:
- Oscillation: aggressive probe cadence causes repeated concurrency changes. Mitigation: add cooldown windows and require sustained signal before persistent change.
- Thermal spike on H100 at high clocks: mitigation: hard fallback to frequency governor profile "sustained-low-boost" and move non-SLA traffic to a lower tier.
- KV memory oversubscription: mitigation: immediate disable coalescing for that worker and mark cache warmup period.

Open experiments / next steps:
- Evaluate fine-grained kernel packing that merges attention heads only when attention compute is the critical path (vs memory bound) using microbenchmarks.
- Explore a lightweight on-device thermal model that predicts temp/power from sequences in the next 5s to prevent harmful probe attempts.
- Quantized kernel trade-offs: measure whether 4-bit kernels reduce power enough to allow higher concurrency on L4 without latency regression.

Rollout checklist (practical):
- Implement PAC telemetry export (Power, Temp, ActiveContexts) and add Console dashboard.
- Add runtime flags and a simple config UI to override per-pool defaults.
- Implement probe scaffolding and safe rollback logic.
- Create test harness for 24/48h lab runs and publish results to linked PR.

Appendix: quick example scenarios (how the runtime behaves):
- Scenario A: A100 serving many KV-hit chat requests. Default base_concurrency=6, KV-hit rate 75% -> runtime increases coalescing_max_batch to 40 via boost, achieves 2.4x throughput improvement for bursts while keeping p99 stable.
- Scenario B: H100 cluster sees sudden mix of cold long-context decodes. Power rises above 90% TDP for 5s -> PAC reduces concurrency by 2, sets governor to sustained-low-boost, and schedules a 30s cooldown. Endpoints remain available; p95 increases slightly but p99 improves compared to thermal-throttled behavior.

Notes and references: link to current kernel scheduler PR and notes above.
